top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) is an invention whose original idea, the magic-wavelength lattice, has been verified by independent Sr, Yb and Hg clocks agreeing at the 1e-18 level, and it opens a door to tests of redshift and constants. The two-name allocation is the cleanest attribution on the slate and the citation can be kept to the invention and demonstrated accuracy. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a strong, verified discovery but the theory-to-experiment credit chain (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu, Hasan) is not settled, so I rank it second. No award is last because there are mature, verified candidates.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague and Mehlig is in the neighbouring Gothenburg department, but no collaboration with either or any tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp
